title: Florida's 26th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: Florida's 26th Congressional District is being contested in the 2026 midterm elections. Incumbent Republican Rep. Mario Díaz-Balart, the longest-serving member of Florida's U.S. House delegation, is seeking re-election in a district redrawn in 2026 that shed Collier County while retaining portions of Miami-Dade County including Doral, Hialeah, and surrounding communities. The district remains Republican-leaning, having voted for Donald Trump by an estimated 18 points under the previous map. Two Democrats—Miami attorney Nicole Locklin and certified public accountant Yurina Gil—competed in the August 18 Democratic primary, with the winner advancing to face Díaz-Balart in the November general election. The race reflects broader national dynamics around congressional control, redistricting, and the strength of Democratic challenges in GOP-leaning South Florida districts.

candidates.name: Mario Díaz-Balart
candidates.summary: Mario Díaz-Balart is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Florida's 26th Congressional District. First elected to Congress in 2002, he previously represented Florida's 21st and 25th districts and is the longest-serving member of the Florida U.S. House delegation. His career has focused on appropriations, foreign affairs, and South Florida constituent issues.

candidates.name: Nicole Locklin
candidates.summary: Nicole Locklin is a Miami attorney and Democratic candidate for U.S. House in Florida's 26th District. A first-generation college graduate and graduate of Santa Clara University School of Law, she has worked as a litigation associate and as an attorney at technology companies including Nextdoor and Databricks. Her campaign focuses on anti-corruption, affordability, healthcare, and civil rights.

candidates.name: Yurina Gil
candidates.summary: Yurina Gil is a Cuban-American certified public accountant and Democratic candidate for U.S. House in Florida's 26th District. Born in Marianao, Cuba, she emigrated to the United States in 1998 and earned degrees from Miami Dade College and Florida International University. Her campaign priorities include affordability, climate resilience, congressional integrity, supply chain diversification, and human rights.
